overview: This file documents the State Department’s management of Japanese and other Axis press representatives from late 1940 through 1942, beginning with the visa dispute over journalist Toichiro Takamatsu and expanding after Pearl Harbor into questions of detention, reciprocal treatment, exchange, and repatriation. Through diplomatic communications involving Japan, Spain, and Switzerland, the papers follow Japanese correspondents held at Hot Springs and Fort Missoula, efforts to protect American journalists in Japanese-controlled territory, and negotiations over exchange-vessel priorities. The file also covers Clarke H. Kawakami’s public break with Japan’s militarist government, individual repatriation cases, and administrative disputes concerning Kyozo Mori’s automobile and missing personal effects.
interest: Journalists as protected civilians and bargaining chips: visas, censorship, detention transfers, property claims, protecting-power talks, and Kawakami's denunciation of Japan.
